name: T-62M (refurbished reserve stock)

placement_rationale.text: T-62M is 1960s-era reserve stock reactivated by attrition rather than a front-line-optimized design — a 115mm rifled gun a full generation behind the 125mm smoothbore standard — so 5 km, toward the rear edge of doctrine.md's lower-sky bracket (1–1.5 km with local air/drone superiority, ~7 km without) rather than its closest end, is consistent with a unit fielding obsolete armor cautiously rather than committing it to the tightest direct-fire positions a modern tank might hold. (Nudged 5→4.6 km from this category's shared round-number value so it doesn't literally coincide with side_b-armor-t-80bvm on the map's distance axis — a small, deterministic spread within the same band, not a new plausibility claim beyond what's already argued above.)

minimal modern electronics even in 'M' refurbishment
Strength: Available in large numbers from deep Soviet-era storage; simple to operate
Limitation: Obsolete armor and firepower by any current standard; withdrawn from Russian active service over a decade before the war, now reactivated purely due to attrition of modern types
Estimated quantity available: Reactivation numbers not precisely disclosed; drawn from a Soviet-era storage pool understood to still hold thousands of pre-1970s AFVs
employment_notes: Direct evidence that wartime attrition has forced Russia into 1960s-era equipment it had formally retired — a stronger illustration of matériel strain than any modern-tank statistic
contrast_vs_traditional: A 1960s-era tank pulled from decades of strategic storage is the clearest illustration of what drone-dominated attrition does to an armour inventory: with drones now widely reported as the leading cause of equipment losses on both sides (the often-quoted 60–70% share is directional reporting, not an audited figure — see the Key Lessons page's caution on selection effect), modern armour is being consumed faster than factories can replace it, so reserve stock built for a different war gets pressed into this one on sheer attritional arithmetic rather than because it is well matched to the threat it will face.
